correctness.rationale: For every positive part size and every nonnegative multiindex, the polytope is exactly the set of nonnegative block coordinates with sum of block maxima at most one. Lebesgue block-maxima density is a Dirichlet(m_1,...,m_r,1) simplex density. Given maxima, each block has one uniformly chosen maximizer and other coordinates independent uniform; multiplying exact conditional powers with Dirichlet rising-factorial moments proves the claimed all-degree rational identity without extrapolation. First and second degrees simplify to exact signed covariances, and the inertia has strictly convex separable polynomial coefficients for N>=2. Balancing and splitting prove both sharp extrema, with one-part and singleton-part boundaries checked. Exact simplex integration from the actual checker path independently matches 17 small part profiles (653 nonzero simplices) and 368 cubic/quartic monomials.

originality.rationale: The comparison covers canonical graph stable-set geometry, general polytope moment generating functions, published complete-multipartite John ellipsoid structure, and centrally symmetric Hanner free sums. The closest relevant result gives the sum-of-maxima representation, but not volume-uniform Dirichlet component laws, the closed multivariate arbitrary-degree moment formula, sign recovery, or strict balancing extremizers. General triangulation methods allow any fixed integration, not this uniform symbolic all-dimension family statement plus exact extremal consequences. No inspected claim logically implies the complete finding without further nontrivial derivation. Older alternative free-sum, join or Dirichlet terminology remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: A pre-existing free-sum-of-convex-cubes integration or Dirichlet-radial-mixture theorem in older literature may imply the all-order formula after a short specialization.
Search and record coverage is not exhaustive; negative database searches are not a priority guarantee.
The full text of the multipartite minimum-sphere result was not necessary to decide that its abstract concerns a different invariant, but its detailed mathematics was not inspected.
Results depend on canonical Euclidean indicator coordinates and interior Lebesgue volume; coordinate changes or a vertex-uniform interpretation alter the covariance signs.

value.rationale: The stable-set polytopes of complete multipartite graphs form a natural infinite 0/1 polytope family with varying part structure. The compact arbitrary-multiindex moment identity determines the entire uniform interior probability law rather than one isolated finite statistic. Its off-diagonal covariance signs exactly reconstruct the defining graph when r>=2; this is a meaningful structural inverse statement. The strictly Schur-convex trace and refinement monotonicity give a complete sharp classification of a natural Euclidean invariant across all integer compositions, with equality cases. These results are not just finite table entries, a known-polytopal-relabeling, or a normalization check, though the derivation uses standard Dirichlet tools.
